title: Oui, huit, fille
intro: French has three quick sounds that glide into the next vowel, the **semi-vowels**: /w/ as in **oui**, /ɥ/ as in **huit**, and /j/ as in **fille**. They turn two vowels into one syllable: *oui* is /wi/, not /u.i/. The hardest one for English speakers is /ɥ/: *lui* /lɥi/ is not *Louis* /lwi/.

cases.label: ou + vowel = /w/
cases.rule: **ou** before another vowel glides into /w/, in one syllable: *oui* /wi/, *jouer* /ʒwe/, *Louis* /lwi/, *ouest* /wɛst/.

cases.label: u + vowel = /ɥ/: huit, lui
cases.rule: **u** before another vowel becomes /ɥ/: round your lips for **u** and slide straight into the next vowel. *huit* /ɥit/, *nuit* /nɥi/, *lui* /lɥi/, *cuisine* /kɥi.zin/, *juin* /ʒɥɛ̃/.

cases.label: i + vowel = /j/
cases.rule: **i** before another vowel becomes /j/, like the English *y* in *yes*: *pied* /pje/, *bien* /bjɛ̃/, *hier* /jɛʁ/, *viande* /vjɑ̃d/, *chien* /ʃjɛ̃/.

cases.label: ill = /ij/: fille
cases.rule: After a consonant, **ill** sounds /ij/, with no /l/: *fille* /fij/, *famille* /fa.mij/, *gentille* /ʒɑ̃.tij/. Three common exceptions keep the /l/: **ville, mille, tranquille**.

cases.label: ail, eil, euil, ouille = /j/
cases.rule: After a vowel, **il** or **ill** is just /j/: *travail* /tʁa.vaj/, *soleil* /sɔ.lɛj/, *feuille* /fœj/, *bouteille* /bu.tɛj/, *grenouille* /ɡʁə.nuj/.

cases.label: y = /j/
cases.rule: **y** before a vowel is /j/: *yeux* /jø/. Between two vowels, it works like **i + i**: *crayon* /kʁɛ.jɔ̃/, *payer* /pe.je/, *voyage* /vwa.jaʒ/.

examples.en: The wind is coming from the west.

sections.title: 3. u + vowel = /ɥ/

examples.en: I'm talking to him in the kitchen.

sections.tip: Compare *lui* /lɥi/ (him) and *Louis* /lwi/ (a name), *huit* /ɥit/ and *oui* /wi/. For /ɥ/, keep your lips round, as for **u**.

sections.title: 4. i + vowel = /j/
sections.tip: Like the *y* in *yes*: *bien* is one syllable.

sections.title: 5. ill = /ij/: fille

examples.fr: Il y a {mille|sv-ill} habitants dans cette petite {ville|sv-ill}.
examples.en: There are a thousand people in this little town.

sections.tip: The exceptions **ville, mille, tranquille** keep their /l/: *une ville tranquille* /vil tʁɑ̃.kil/.

sections.title: 6. ail, eil, euil, ouille

examples.en: The sun is shining on the leaves.

sections.tip: After a vowel, you never hear an /l/: *soleil* ends with /j/, like *yes* without the *es*.

sections.title: 7. y = /j/

examples.en: We have to pay for the trip.

sections.tip: Between two vowels, **y** = **i + i**: *crayon* sounds like *crai-ion*.

mistakes.why: **u** + vowel is /ɥ/, with round lips, not /w/.
**ville, mille, tranquille** are exceptions: you hear the /l/.

story.title: Huit, pas oui !
story.en: The Easter holidays: Tom visits Léa and Lou, and a little girl gives him a pronunciation lesson.

lines.fr: Pendant les vacances de Pâques, Tom vient voir Léa et Lou. Lou veut jouer à compter.
lines.en: During the Easter holidays, Tom comes to see Léa and Lou. Lou wants to play counting.

lines.fr: Un, deux, {trois|sv-oi}, quatre, cinq, six, sept, {huit|sv-u} !
lines.en: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight!
Well done, Lou! Me too: six, seven… yes!

lines.fr: Pour « {huit|sv-u} », Tom, il faut faire une petite bouche ronde, comme pour « tu ».
lines.en: For 'huit', Tom, you have to make a small round mouth, as for 'tu'.

lines.fr: Non ! Écoute bien : « {lui|sv-u} », « {Louis|sv-ou} ». Ce n'est pas pareil !
lines.en: No! Listen carefully: 'lui', 'Louis'. They're not the same!

lines.fr: Regarde, Tom : une petite {fille|sv-ill}, sa {famille|sv-ill}, le {soleil|sv-ail} et une {abeille|sv-ail} !
lines.en: Look, Tom: a little girl, her family, the sun and a bee!

lines.fr: Une {fille|sv-ill}… et une {ville|sv-ill} ? On dit pareil ?
lines.en: A girl… and a town? Do you say them the same?

lines.fr: Non, écoute : « {fille|sv-ill} », « {ville|sv-ill} ». Ce n'est pas pareil ! Et « {ville|sv-ill} », c'est comme « {mille|sv-ill} » et « {tranquille|sv-ill} ».
lines.en: No, listen: 'fille', 'ville'. They're not the same! And 'ville' is like 'mille' and 'tranquille'.

lines.fr: Et le {soleil|sv-ail} a des {yeux|sv-y} ! Je l'ai fait avec mon {crayon|sv-y} jaune.
lines.en: And the sun has eyes! I did it with my yellow pencil.

lines.fr: Bon, il est {huit|sv-u} heures. Au lit, Lou !
lines.en: Right, it's eight o'clock. Bedtime, Lou!

lines.fr: Tom, tu me racontes une histoire de {chien|sv-i} ?
lines.en: Tom, will you tell me a story about a dog?

lines.fr: Il était une fois un {chien|sv-i} qui avait {huit|sv-u} amis, et qui {voyageait|sv-y} toute la {nuit|sv-u}…
lines.en: Once upon a time, there was a dog who had eight friends, and who travelled all night…

lines.fr: Lou rit. Après trois histoires, elle dort enfin. Tom dit tout bas : « Bonne {nuit|sv-u}, Lou ! »
lines.en: Lou laughs. After three stories, she's finally asleep. Tom says quietly: 'Good night, Lou!'

quiz.q: To say the u in « nuit », your lips are…
In which word do you hear an /l/?
Listen: do you hear an /l/ at the end?
